Acid rain happens when pollutants like sulfur dioxide (SO₂) and nitrogen oxides (NOₓ)—mainly from burning fossil fuels in power plants, vehicles, and industry—react in the atmosphere with water vapor. They form sulfuric and nitric acids, which then fall as rain, snow, or even dry particles.
It’s a serious environmental issue because it:
Damages forests and crops
Acidifies lakes and harms aquatic life
Erodes buildings and monuments
Contributes to respiratory problems in humans
